source.title: Unlearning of Knowledge Graph Embedding via Preference Optimization
source.authors: Jiajun Liu; Wenjun Ke; Peng Wang; Yao He; Zi-Yu Shang; Guozheng Li; Zijie Xu; Ke Ji

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates unlearning in knowledge graph embedding models, not recovery attacks on unlearned LLMs. It neither tests a listed claim version nor uses the LLM recovery finding as a tool or assumption.
record.gate_note: The paper reports GraphDPO results for KGE link prediction, including lower performance on forgotten triples. It does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation-direction edits, quantization, prompt-based recovery, or resistance to those attacks. Its discussion of LLM unlearning does not report new results about the claim.
record.test_reason: The study proposes GraphDPO for unlearning in knowledge graph embedding (TransE etc.) models, not LLMs. It runs no recovery attack: no relearning fine-tune, no activation ablation, no quantization, no prompting. It reports only its own method's forgetting/retention MRR against baselines. It neither tests nor uses the shallow-unlearning finding. It mentions inference of forgotten triples from remaining ones only as motivation and never measures it as recovery.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude GraphDPO forgets target triples while preserving remaining and boundary knowledge. It beats approximate baselines by up to 10.1% MRR_Avg and 14.0% MRR_F1, and trains faster.
record.recipe_differences: GraphDPO reframes KGE unlearning as preference optimization and adds out-boundary sampling and boundary-aware recall; it is not a test of the cited LLM unlearning recipes or their recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that forgetting performance varies across datasets and time steps; it does not test sensitivity to recovery-attack settings.

fits_no_version.finding: GraphDPO reduces MRR on forgotten triples by 10%-50% relative to the pre-trained KGE model across datasets, while retaining more remaining-set MRR than most approximate baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preference-optimization unlearning in KGE models lowers link-prediction performance on forgotten triples while preserving boundary knowledge; says nothing about recoverability.

record.problems: The reported forgetting summary is an aggregate range across datasets, with no uncertainty estimate stated for that result. The paper studies KGE rather than LLM recovery attacks.
record.rows_left_out: Other KGE metrics, models, datasets, baselines, and ablations were not extracted because they do not test any listed recovery version and are not needed for the aggregate finding recorded in R1.

untested.parts: No LLM; no test of whether simple attacks recover forgotten knowledge.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack after unlearning.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion.
No prompting, rephrasing, jailbreak or in-context recovery.
GraphDPO is not tested against any recovery attack.

record.verdict_notes: The record says peer_reviewed 'The Web Conference'. The text calls itself a preprint under review and names no venue; treat as not stated. The record's T6/discusses classification is correct.

versions.untested_parts: No LLM unlearning or attack-recovery test; it does not test whether simple attacks recover targeted knowledge.
No post-unlearning relearning or fine-tuning attack.
No activation-direction ablation or test of access blocking versus deletion.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery test.
GraphDPO is proposed for KGE unlearning; the study does not test resistance to the listed recovery attacks.

rows.subject: GraphDPO
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated link-prediction performance on forgotten triples after GraphDPO optimization, compared with the original pre-trained models.
rows.value: Performance decreases by 10%-50% on all datasets
rows.note: The paper gives this as an across-dataset summary; it does not report values for each dataset in the text. This is KGE forgetting performance, not recovery after an attack.
rows.check: KGE link-prediction MRR on forgotten triples for the study's own method versus the pre-trained model. It is a method-performance result, not a recovery-attack result. The subject is a KGE model, not an LLM. The state 'partial' has no referent version; set to cannot_determine. Subject kind is a method applied to TransE, not a model.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
